headline: RACER reports role-based competence estimates for routing to unseen human experts
summary: A September 18 work-in-progress preprint proposes RACER, which estimates an unseen expert’s query-level probability of being correct from a small context set using class-role relationships rather than absolute class identities. The authors prove a coherent class-relabelling invariance result, derive a Bayes-aligned deferral surrogate and provide a regret bound. In experiments, they report gains on synthetic expert benchmarks and budget-swept performance described as competitive or best on VinDr-CXR and CheXpert. On CheXpert, RACER-C and RACER-kernel report similar primary AURSBAC means (0.7243 and 0.7241 over 27 matched cells); the paper labels the comparisons descriptive and makes no significance claim. VinDr-CXR results use training annotations because official test labels lack radiologist identities; an out-of-distribution expert group is inferred from co-annotation patterns. Results remain author-reported and the code is not yet released.
